history.period: Legendary/ancient; the present shrine is a small stone temple at the lake
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED - but DISTINCT FROM THE SIKH GURDWARA: the Lakshman (Lokpal) Temple is an ancient Hindu shrine on the banks of Hemkund Lake (traditionally called Lokpal Jheel by the people of the Bhyundar Valley), roughly 100 metres from Gurdwara Sri Hemkund Sahib - it is NOT part of the gurdwara. Local Hindu tradition holds that Lakshmana (Sheshnag) performed penance/meditation here, in one version to regain his strength after defeating Meghnad; King Pandu is also said to have meditated at the lake. The gurdwara is a separate, much later (20th-century) Sikh shrine devoted to Guru Gobind Singh, established after Sant Sohan Singh identified Lokpal Lake with the site described in the Dasam Granth in the 1930s. Both pilgrimage sites now share the lake. ELEVATION CONFLICT: sources report the lake/site at 4,632 m (Wikipedia/Indiapost) and 4,329 m (Curly Tales, 2026 reopening report; sahasa.in: 14,200 ft) - verify. Coordinates are the Hemkund settlement/lake pin (30.69902, 79.6148); the temple itself is ~100 m from the gurdwara (verify exact pin).

name: Lakshman Temple, Hemkund (Lokpal Laxman Temple)
town: Hemkund Sahib (on the banks of Hemkund/Lokpal Lake, ~100 m from the gurdwara)
town_description: Hemkund (Lokpal Jheel) is a glacial lake high in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, ringed by seven snow-clad peaks of the Saptashringa/Saptarishi range and Hathi Parvat. It is one of the rare shared pilgrimage sites of two faiths: Gurdwara Sri Hemkund Sahib, the Sikh shrine devoted to Guru Gobind Singh, stands on its banks alongside the ancient Hindu Lokpal Lakshman temple. The site is reached only by the steep trek from Ghangaria/Govindghat and opens for a few months each year.

travel.road: Road to Govindghat, then ~19 km trek (or helicopter Govindghat-Ghangaria, then ~5-6 km trek) to Hemkund - per euttaranchal.com
